text_clean: At the moment, for me personally, I don't see things changing much. I do think that overall, AI will get *better* at the things that I'm already using it to do—brainstorming, research, editing—and that will be a boon overall.

When I think of AI at its best, it is a tool that helps facilitate broader ideas and eases the burden of life's mundane tasks. I can understand why some feel that it's perhaps a "threat" to artistic endeavours and that it will replace artists in creative mediums. However, I am optimistic that human creativity will always triumph and that AI can work alongside our efforts to create even better and more meaningful work.

As a tool, I see AI being used for similar things that I use it for now. I think the brainstorming help it provides is very useful. I think it can evolve a bit and play more of a role as an educator for a new grad or someone starting out a getting a feel for the work for the first time.

I'm definitely driving the creative decisions. It was my idea to begin with, the AI just helped me streamline the process so I could get to the fun part quicker. I am very cautious of keeping the creativity mine. I'm worried about AI taking humanity from the arts so I try to use AI as little as possible.
Oh, I am, absolutely, I don't really approach AI when stuck creatively, but rather when stuck in terms of something logistical, or in giving definition to a creative idea.

I do think that I will continue to use it as my icing. It is truly helpful. However, if I hear word from the artist community that we need to make an effort to stop AI use, I'll happily comply. I don't want to be a part of something that ultimately reduces the value of human creativity.

I think, for my given occupation, it'll stay about the same. I think AI will continue to grow and get smarter as we continue to train it, so maybe I'll end up with things like strong titles without a lot of back and forth that starts with some more cheesy ideas. However, like I said, I wish to remain the creative powerhouse of the situation, so I'm not sure I'd ever just blindly take something AI created and slap it on my work as my own. I'd want to keep using it as a tool to get my creative juices flowing, not letting it create for me. Who knows, maybe there will be even more ways in the next couple years that it can assist me without giving up my creative edge, which will allow me to expand on how I use it.

I think it can simplify the aspects of the work that may seem tedious or boring, and take away the creative spark. Stuff like organising outlines, grammar editing, research. Of course, one should always back up AI research with additional insights, including from experts in fields, but it still saves time and effort. It can be a beneficial helper, which promotes critical thinking and gives an author a more holistic view of what it means to be an author in this day and age. It makes one more aware of everything external outside of pure creaitivty and passion.

Could see leaning into more practical implementations of AI as opposed to creative. For example, being able to generate a call sheet based on various factors or being able to filter through a number of grant/funding opportunities to determine which ones would be appropriate for our current project. In terms of the creative side, I don't see that changing for me personally. I don't feel the need to use it currently and it's hard to imagine what would lead to that changing.

As I mentioned above, we've already found some great tools that can help us accomplish bigger things and take on projects that once would have been too big to tackle. So my team and I are open to exploring and dancing with new AI tools when we find the right ones that work with our aesthetic and process. We'll retain our artistic control, but use what tools we can to get us to the end goals more efficiently. I'll be interested to see what we can accomplish using these tools over time.
I drive the creative decisions, AI has been quite disappointing in the creative department. The responses are generic and contrived,
It is really important to me. Unfortunately, I do not think that other feel the same way and I think lines will continue to be blurred.

Because of my own thoughts about AI and the way it impacts workers in creative spaces, I lead the creative process primarily. I will occasionally ask for a list of ideas from the AI, but I almost always turn the conversation towards business planning or research.

I use AI primarily to do the "boring stuff" or use it as a "sounding board". I very rarely ever use AI to generate unique ideas or concepts. Rather I prefer to use it to tell my ideas to and to try to identify gaps or inconsistencies in my own work, as a third person perspective to look at my own output from a different angle.

I always try to drive creative decisions. For me, I like to use it to hone ideas I have already worked on rather than developing ideas. Where it comes in more useful creatively is asking targeted questions about the reality of a situation - the information I can glean from these conversations might make me approach a scene, a beat or an entire arc differently if I find out my assumptions were correct, and so it can guide creativity in that way, but only as a result of using it to interrogate my own awareness and assumptions.

I would say I was driving the creative decisions because I was inputting all of my own ideas; I just needed some help untangling the different aspects of things, such as the themes, the aesthetic, and the sound. The AI was certainly an aid, but I didn't pull straight up AI ideas from it.

Well hopefully the art community will have a more concrete opinion on AI and its role in the field by then. Right now, it feels controversial and harmful. I think the business applications will only continue to improve. As for the creative side, I can see myself using AI in editing aspects, but I don't think AI should ever replace the human element of creating something.

I sadly see it taking over more than it should. I think people will get lazy and let the AI do the work for them. I also think there will be groups of "purists" who will fight it with everything they have in them to keep the true creativity alive. I can see online articles and magazines taking the easy, and cheaper way out and using AI to create content instead of paying people.
I've thought about it a bit but I prefer to work with AI and use it to better myself instead of competing.
I think I will continue to use it the way I have. I hope in the future, the AI will improve and thus improve my performance at work as well.
That's something I have thought about, but I guess my focus has been on learning new skills, including how to work with AI effectively, that will still be needed in the future.

I think working with AI is more likely to help me improve my own skills. I work independently for most of the workday, and it's nice to have AI to bounce ideas around with and to collaborate with to generate the best possible version of a task. I don't think I would like to completely delegate tasks to AI because I worry that my competency with certain skills might decline over time due to lack of practice.

That all depends on what path my company decides to take as AI becomes more prevalent in the workplace. If my company decides to officially support certain AI models and integrate them into our work, I will be happy to use its assistance with more complicated tasks.

I don't think I'd widen the way I use it any time soon. I'm very keen to maintain my knowledge and I guess I see over-reliance on AI as a way to diminish what I know? It's useful for efficiency so I may utilise it in that way in the future (e.g., search my emails, respond to this, etc.), but in terms of finance-specific work I don't want to rely on AI and then find that I struggle with concepts or practices I otherwise would have forced myself to learn.
As it gets better I will lean on it more and more to help me with tasks. I see it being useful for a lot more collaboration as it can handle more complexity.

I think it's very important. I think over the next few years people who don't want to/can't use AI in their work are going to get squeezed out of certain workplaces, because people who can successfully use AI will be able to automate a lot of their work, freeing up their time for higher level work and creative thinking so they will be the high flyers

My job as a [REDACTED] is largely physical, so I'm not worried about losing the major part of my job to AI. Where I can work with AI I'm keen to do so, as it frees up my time to do important conservation repairs etc. which I really enjoy

I think I will be moving to use AI more in the future, especially as it keeps improving. I definitely see myself expanding into new areas and have actually really been enjoying AI in my spare time simply as a learning tool. It makes information extremely accessible, and is able to provide examples instantly.
I think my relationship with AI at work will continue to evolve and flourish. I will continue to use it for more complex tasks, and it will help me achieve the goals and results I need.

I dont plan to use AI much more than I do currently - I think it has its place and it's interesting to learn how it works. It has been useful for answering questions and providing ideas in both my personal life and my career but I dont think I will use it for anything other than factual questions etc in my next career either

I look forward to see the AI models grow and learn, the more up to date they are the more I can rely on the most accurate information and ultimately provide the end-users the best experience possible. I really see myself using AI the same as it is now, we actually do weekly sessions with supply chain discussing the future of AI and how to envolve it within our workflows

I feel as if maintaining certain skills that AI can essentially automate is going to be really difficult and I have found I have to have a balance of using AI and not just so I don't lose out on being able to effectively think freely.

I imagine that I will continue to use AI, probably more and more frequently at work, especially as new models come out and evolve. I am embracing it where it makes sense to, and trying to stay up to date on the best ways to use it professionally.
I envision using AI in lots of different ways to make my job easier and my time more efficiently
I can't really see AI taking over my job. My work is too varied and there is a lot of interpersonal information that must be applied.

It will continue as a double-edged sword for a while. I'll be somewhat reluctant in some respects, but I'll also embrace the positive aspects - I think that it will be necessary in order to stay relevant and ahead of the curve.

it's definitely something I consider. I want to maintain my skills anyway, because anyone who is genuinely a solid user of AI is using it as a partner, not a crutch. I need to still understand the research and tools that the AI is drawing from so that I know when to question, how something can be made better, and when AI misses altogether.

I actively consider in so much as it frees me up to develop or hone my skills in other areas. I see opportunity in building my capability on how to utilise AI as a much more sensible thing to do rather than compete with it. To me it is no different as to how I rely on the expertise and experience of my team and my role is to pull out those strengths rather than compete with them

I feel that I would use it more in my work day, it might even take over certain steps for me, allowing me to dedicate time during the day to other areas. So I feel positive about the near future and what that might look like for me.
I feel like I will continue to use AI at work and seems like it gets better continuously. I would probably use it more if it gets better at writing code.

I will continue to learn what it is good at, and what to avoid, and continue as is for the foreseeable future. If/when the AI companies develop more "integrate-able" solutions, for laypeople like me, I will adopt them. I look forward to that day and continue to try new offerings, and keep abreast so that I can use the latest features as they become available.
It's not really something I actively consider, my work is creating AI. I'm not particularly scared of it taking over because I see all of its flaws

I can see my relationship with AI becoming more dependant. I don't neccesarily want it but the corporate side of the work I do is always looking for buzz words and asking how we could use AI for this, that and the other. I think I'll end up using it more in daily life. We use it to take notes in meetings already
I will always maintain my skills and not solely rely on AI
maybe it'll evolve as AI gets more advanced and can handle more nuances but right now it'll probably stay the same
not really if i'm being honest i'm not too concerned about AI taking over
I can see my use of AI at work expanding in the future. There are probably (definitely) ways to use AI to make my work better/easier/smoother that I haven't thought of yet.

I'll continue using AI for sure. It (usually) helps me save time, and as it gets better and saves me even more time, that's time that I can use to coach more clients, work on my own professional improvement in other areas, or even just relax.
I try to stay knowledgeable in AI technology and capabilities. If and when it becomes part of my position, I will embrace AI and utilize my experiences and knowledge of AI to my advantage.

I see it becoming more integrated with my life. I've also been a curious person and thrive when I'm learning new things. AI is a wealth of knowledge at my hands and why wouldn't I use it. Specifically related to work, I see using it to expand my skillset into areas of interest that I wouldn't be able to reach if I didn't have AI to guide me there.

I am personally a very motivated individual, and I feel I would definitely resist the temptation to let my skills dissipate as AI is used more. If an AI tool can take over perhaps the more menial aspsects of the job allowing me to focus on more advanced areas, then that works for me. But I definitely don't like the idea of losing out on areas to develop and learn because an AI tool is already responsible for that particular job.

I think I will only ever use it for repetitive boring tasks, like I said I really enjoy completing the design process myself. I would possibly consider using it for design ideas if I was stuck, for example asking for text based descriptions of logo ideas and creating them myself.
Not really, in my role I feel that if AI could take over some of my tasks, that would just mean there would be more I could do in other areas.

I expect my relationship with AI at work to continue to grow. As I learn more about what it is capable of doing, I look forward to it making my job easier. I view AI as tool to make me more efficient. The more quickly I can produce quality work with the help of AI, the more I can focus on contributing in other ways and gaining more experience on the job.

I am constantly improving my skills or learning new ones. I feel this is important in order to work collaboratively with AI. The output provided by AI still needs to be reviewed for accuracy and efficacy. So it is necessary for me to remain knowledgeable. That way I can create the right types of prompts and check the information provided by AI.
I consider AI a useful tool, and I can't troubleshoot without tools

Its a good point and it is something I often think about. For me Ai is a great support tool and I don't want to lose my underlying skills as a planning engineer. From time to time I make a conscious effort to do certain things manually, for example I'll still build trackers in excel from scratch and often cross check jobs myself if the dataset is small and AI doesn't seem as time saving.

potentially, I'm not really sure. I hope that AI can do the more borign stuff so that I can do more of what I love. I think poeople get gneuine fulfillment out of their jobs, and I don't want to be in a workplace wher emost of the work is produced by robots, I think I'd find that pretty depressing.

As a fairly creative minded person, I personally don't worry about losing my skills because of AI as I still enjoy it and I work with the AI to create social media captions which keeps my skills involved as well as using AI.
No, its not because I know AI is constantly evolving and I evolve with it. If AI can do something better than me, that's great. There are plenty of skills AI isn't great with that I can learn.

Of course! As I continue to refine my skills at using AI, I have no doubt I will find new ways to implement. For example, I am currently trying to figure out a way to integrate it into our yard management system to auto generate trailer reports and send them to vendors at the start and end of shifts to ensure we don't have gridlock in our shipping yard
I do not see myself expanding my use of AI at this point. I think the most I will get out of it in my career is simply the streamlining of tasks I already do without it, as I mentioned before.

At the minute I think I'll use it the same way, perhaps even less when I get more familiar in the kitchen and better with time management. On the other hand though, when i'm trusted with more work load as well as more difficult stuff i'll end up going back to it again.

I believe my use of AI will continue to grow, as models improve I may feel less sceptical of how it well it works and may start using it for more complicated tasks. But as it stands currently I still feel that is a long way away

I'm very aware that my line of work could be replaced by AI entirely, but I've also spent a lot of time fixing things which were AI generated and did not work correctly. I believe maintaining my skills are important and will remain relevant at least in the short to medium term as AI still is not perfect and continues to need manual intervention

I don't really have this concern or consider this too much. AI can help with my job, but likely would not be able to take over my job. I keep my skills and knowledge up to date, but I never really worry about AI interfering down the road.

I've tailored how I like to use AI to suit my needs for now. One way it could potentially evolve is if accuracy became less of a concern then it could maybe become more helpful with detailed/financial related tasks in the future.
To be honest I don't think much about it. If there's some aspects AI do well, then I will switch my focus to other areas.
It is and is major reason I am embracing using AI to make me focus on the important stuff.
It's always important to maintain your skillset, if your favorite AI model breaks or you have no internet, you need to rely on yourself

I don't really think about maintaining my skills where AI agents could potentially automate that work. It will happen eventually, and I maintain my skills through the work that I do on a day to day basis.
It will start to become more 'embedded' in my work, like, automatic, and part of the standard procedures, as opposed to now when it is more an 'extra'.

AI is very good at dealing with things already there, but not so good at coming up with new ones. So, as I learn more ways to use AI to free up my own time and energy, I can develop new ideas and processes that make our overall business run better. Getting bogged down in some tasks takes away time that could go into improving everything.

I think maximising my ability in using AI to do these tasks is key as while AI is going to take over these jobs becoming an expert in AI usage where and how it can be used is rather key and in the medium term I imagine would have key career benefits. Once it fully takes over it will be a much tougher situation, so being able to adapt and find a niche working within the AI is key.
AI taking over is a myth. I'd be more concern about people lagging behind and stopping using their brains and creative power.

I love creative work. And AI can help make it less stagnant. Plus it is a big helper already in implementing different ideas, in coding specifically. Working more efficiently and less time, spending more on developing management and leadership qualities rather then just simple "do you work" approach.

yes I definetley consider that, for me I think it is more about learning to work with it and be happy where it can take over stressful or annoying tasks - I want to be able to focus more on strategy and development so it works well
Not really, if I am being honest. I like using AI, and it does help make things easier at times, to give me more time to myself, or for other ventures.

I think my company may eventually incorporate AI into our products to some extent and, so, the skills I have developed with AI in recent times, will be of great use to the company as a whole. I think as we move forward, I will continue to use AI in the way that I am doing, but the results will get better and I will become more efficient with my time and possibly have more time for other projects and helping the company in other ways.
I hope to continue to use it more and more for tasks I see as boring and rote - for example, grading homework or labs.
I like to think of AI as my assistant, not my replacement.

To be honest I haven't really considered that; it isn't often that I need to do something like the example above where I can't really contribute to the process. I'd just envision me using it more and more, ever forming a closer 'relationship'. The more time I can save here and there with AI efficiencies, the more time I will have during the working week to look at strategic goals and the bigger picture, and involve my AI colleague with this to help me continue to improve and take my department forward.

I feel like the best thing I can do in maintaining my skills is learning how to utilize Ai efficiently. I don't think that Ai will ever fully replace my job because I have to think about the human aspect of it. I have to speak and try to influence others to agree with my stance, which Ai can't do.
No, it's not something I've thought about. My line of work isn't particularly swift in adapting new technology so I feel like it would take a long time until we would be in that position
i consider it, but am not actively working on it
I think i will rely more and more on it until it is most of my job
As it stands I don't see my daily use of AI changing very much, though I appreciate that the technology is rapidly improving.

I think my use of AI will remain pretty much the same. The only reason I would use it less is if the quality of the AI responses becomes drastically worse, to the point where they are no longer helpful. Otherwise, I use it about as much as I would like.
Sometimes I think about losing skills because AI is doing it for me. But I do a lot of writing on my own as well so I feel that helps keep my skills
I imagine I will use it more as it gets better and better.

i am not worried about AI taking over, i feel like i keep improving my skills anyway and i have the capability to work alongside of AI, i see AI as a great helping tool which is bound to make a lot of things easier but i do strongly believe that it is important to have people alongised that are capable to understand and use it correctly, you know we all get things wrong sometimes even AI
i do think my relationship with AI at work is evolving as AI progresses and new functions are brought out i can use it for new different things

I believe that the capabilities of AI models have reached a plateau and I do not expect to see extreme developments in the coming years. Sure, models might get more training data, or be more powerful in terms of performance, but I don't expect a fundamental change in them. Consequently, I don't expect any major change in how I use AI at work. I have spent quite some time working with various models, understanding their capabilities and limitations, as well as fine-tuning my approach on how to utilize them effectively. Currently, I believe that I have reached a satisfactory level, where AI saves me time and allows me to be more productive at work, which is the relationship I expect to continue having for some time ahead.
I don't really know - maybe just more everywhere? I suppose I'll come to rely on it more heavily as it becomes better at understanding prompts from someone struggling to understand a problem.

I want to maintain my relationship with AI in the same way I do now- using it as a tool to assist me, helping me balance the mental load of tasks that could be done in a more efficient manner, while also maintaining a critical awareness of its overuse. I think balance is the key to everything, and using AI should be no different. I will definitely keep using it as I have been!

No, I haven't considered AI being able to take over what I do. I see it has enhancing productivity, but I do not think it can fully take over as there is also a personal aspect and customer/client relationship we maintain. I have many responsibilities/duties in my job. Besides troubleshooting, I do continuing education and advanced training with our clients. Modern and larger labs are often quite automated now with a track system, but troubleshooting issues and hardware issues will require us to be at a client site in person.

It is not something I actively consider. A lot of my job is reacting to situations on the fly and planning and big picture "stuff." I have a hard time imagining AI taking over a lot of what I do. Now, were I to become confident enough in AI to let it do research and such for me, maintaining skills would have to be an active and proactive process, as it is a perishable skill.

Probably about the same, perhaps a bit more. When using AI, it's often as a matter of it being in front of me at the right time rather than thinking "hey, this is a project I can do with AI." I more often use integrated tools.

I sometimes feel like AI has already taken over in areas of my job and it feels pointless to maintain these skills and like I should just invest in learning new skills. I think it's more worth investing in skills that AI isn't that good at, like handling complex instructions and coming up with unique ideas.

I do not believe AI will ever be able to take over my work. There is too much human touch that is required for that to be possible. However, in certain aspects, I believe AI could be a helpful aide to people in my profession.

I don't think about it. I've been at this a long time and feel comfortable with where I am. My skills will always be sharp and if I feel I could improve on anything, I will do so in a way that they are my own skills that I don't need to rely on anything for.

Honestly, the capabilities of AI and the speed at which they were progressing was starting to become a bit scary. However, over the past couple of months the breakthroughs appear to have slowed down, so I feel a bit more secure in my job now. The tasks I do are still not fully automate-able, so as of now it seems that my relationship with AI will remain the same - using it as a collaborative tool to complete my tasks.
I'm trying to become more skilled in using AI to help with tasks that I know it's good at so that I can focus on the more high value tasks that I use at work.
I'm definitely trying to get on more varied projects but I don't think AI could do my job fully. There would always need to be some human element to it
I do not see it changing much in the foreseeable future. The only way I am current expanding my AI usage is through daily planning.

As a young student I've adapted to use AI to learn subjects and grow with it, so I don't really worry about it taking over my skillset, but more so how I can develop with it and become more efficient.

I see my relationship evolving as I learn how to integrate it more and more throughout my business where it can do equally as well as I would or outperform my skillset in a certain task. My goal is to essentially have the best output with minimal effort.
I don't actively consider AI taking over in any areas in my field. It does not seem to be in the near future, at least to me
I can see AI still being used in communications at work and maybe being used for tasks that do not need human intervention, which can make my job easier.

I personally find AI helps me learn quickly. Instead of searching stack overflow for ages trying to figure stuff out, I can ask AI and get the answer plus an explanation. I want to use it to automate the simpler tasks as much as possible while I fill in the more complex parts and fit everything together

I hope that my employment will look to explore ways to incorporate AI positively into our workday. It would be nice to see AI utilised to streamline these processes and push the boundaries of ambition.

I do think about this and I do try to challenge myself to not hand over every task I can to AI. I want to be able to write original content quickly without the use of AI, if needed. That said, it's probably clear from my responses that I think AI needs to be managed and used critically in order to optimize it's results. Due to that, I still think AI will need "me" as a "manager" for tasks going forward.

I anticipate continuing to work with AI. I think I'll get better at writing meaningful prompts to get the "most" out of my work with AI. I also think the AI will improve and "learn" my needs better, which is something I look forward to.

For the time being, I don't see my use of AI changing very much. I am pretty comfortable with the way I am using it now. And I am not sure if my employer plans to use or implement any AI tools into our day to day operations and tasks.

I haven't given much thought to it, but in general I don't want to completely rely on AI for all my writing and communication needs. As I am always trying to improve my own skills. However at times using AI can help me with ideas on how to phrase things, or organize emails for the future so I may not always have to ask for help with certain things.

I have considered this, and I still don't have a good answer. I think at this point in time AI is still more of a collaborative tool so employees still need their skills in order for a company to be successful. In the future that might not be the case, but I like to understand how things work so I think I will always want to understand how the model is doing things and maintain my skills just because I want to understand.

I expect AI to take on more of the day to day administrative tasks while I focus more on the big picture items. I expect it to continue to be a collaboration, but I do think AI will be handling more of the most time consuming tasks.

I am genuinely not concerned about AI taking over my work! So much of my work is people-facing, and the parts that aren't simply require a level of real-world judgment I trust the executive board to know better than to hand over to algorithms.
I always keep on top of all my skills. Although AI might take over, it doesn't always do things correctly so I need to be able to understand how to fix the AI code when it isnt correct.

I'm not too worried about it. AI is an incredible tool, but working with it has made me very aware of its limitations. I don't think it will take over any role I'm in completely, provided I'm willing to stay flexible and learn new things.
I hope to transfer more routine tasks to AI and to be able to collaborate more closely to complete work goals more quickly and therefore reach more of my work goals.

I have known some who despair and look at their skills as being made less valuable due to AI, but I prefer to instead see it as an opportunity to enhance those skills I already have and treat it as a sort of challenge. If an AI can do something, then I believe should see that as a starting point and try to be able to do more. I do however acknowledge that AI models will probably always be faster than I can be and sometimes "good enough" is sufficient in work contexts so getting better can seem to lack a benefit. The existence and popularity of AI is therefore a motivation to broaden my skills.

It's something I've considered, but a lot of my business is networking and talking with other people. So the only part I feel like that could be taken over with AI is the routine maintenance and admin work which as a freelancer actually protects my business more than anything because it gives me more time to do the actual business work of networking and working with clients instead of sitting in front of a computer all day.

I need to make an effort to learn and understand more about what AI can do in my current role. I also see that a big part of my role will then be leading and helping people adapt to AI - my role is to lead change and I see a lot of this being driven by AI. One other aspect I see is the need for people and organisations to build up trust for AI and what it can do before it can be widely adopted.
i think I will continue to use it and refine the ways I use it to make it work for me and what I need to get out of it
not really, I have not put much thought into it.

AI is currently helping me grow my communication and negotiation skills, so as I improve in those areas I hope to change to be less dependent in those areas and learn new ways to interact. In a sense, once I have a better foundation, I hope to use more advanced techniques and ask more in-depth questions to grow even further.

Again, I believe AI is a great tool to be used in conjunction with people instead of replacing people outright.
